title: Caramelised Apple Star Crêpes with Apple Butter Sauce
changes_from_base: Not a thin flour-and-milk crêpe: a small, rich cream batter is poured over a star of browned apple slices in the pan and turned out apple side up, with a quick apple-juice butter sauce instead of sugar and lemon.
summary: Delicate single-serve crêpes with a caramelised apple star cooked right into the batter, finished with a buttery apple sauce.

ingredients.item: large tart apple (Granny Smith or Golden Delicious), about 220 g

steps.title: Prep apple
steps.text: Peel, core and quarter 1 large tart apple, then cut each quarter into 4 slices to give 16 pieces.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Boil 120 ml apple juice with 2 tbsp caster sugar in a small saucepan until reduced by half, about 5 min.

steps.title: Enrich sauce
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in 28 g cold butter a few cubes at a time until glossy, then keep warm without letting it boil again.

steps.title: Make batter
steps.text: Whisk 4 tsp flour with 4 tsp caster sugar, 1 egg and ¼ tsp vanilla, then beat in 120 ml double cream until smooth.

steps.title: Brown apples
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp butter in a 20 cm pan and brown 4 apple slices on both sides, then arrange them in the centre as a star.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour a quarter of the batter evenly over the apple star, keeping it in place, and cook for about 1 min until lightly browned underneath and fully set.

steps.title: Turn out
steps.text: Turn the crêpe onto a warm plate so the apple sits on top, then repeat with the remaining batter and apple to make 4.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Spoon a little warm sauce over each crêpe before serving.

tips: Brown the apple slices well before pouring over the batter, as they won't cook much further once covered.
Keep the sauce warm rather than letting it reboil, or it may separate once the cold butter is whisked in.
Cook each crêpe until the batter is completely set before turning it out, so the apple star holds together on top.
storage: These crêpes are best served immediately while warm, so make them just before your guests sit down. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
